header.what: One run of Klaxon's diagnosis agent on the case duplicate-delivery: claude-opus-5-5 through Claude Code on Aravind's seat (live). Its tools read incident data captured from Klaxon's live stack.

diagnosis.hypothesis:
ledger-consumer was recreated at 07:41:36Z with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive, 30 s before the alert. That handler books every Kafka message and never checks whether an event_id was already posted. The provider resends webhooks until they are acknowledged, and webhook-receiver queues each delivery as a new message, so one event can sit at several offsets (evt_000308 at 2@95-97). Each copy became its own ledger transaction.

The extras add up to the alert exactly. Four payments were booked twice: $134.47. One $8.75 refund was booked three times: -$17.50. Net: +$116.97.

The ledger stays balanced because each duplicate is a full double-entry transaction. Payments and refunds still match the provider, so the fault is in ledger posting only.

Still open: which handler ran before 07:41:36, and why the provider redelivered (normal retries or slow acknowledgements).

evidence.shows: The symptom is real. evt_000288, 298, 352 and 373 were each posted twice, and evt_000308 three times. The ledger is +$116.97 against the provider. The ledger is balanced, and payments and refunds match the provider.
ledger-consumer was redeployed at 07:41:36Z with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive. Every other service was deployed at 07:39.
ledger-consumer posted evt_000308 three times at 07:41:50, from offsets 2@95, 2@96 and 2@97, each with a different trace_id.
webhook-receiver queued evt_000308 three times between 07:41:41 and 07:41:43, at offsets 95-97: repeated provider deliveries of the same event.
ledger-consumer logged no 'duplicate' line in the last 15 minutes, so it never skipped a redelivered event.
evt_000288 was posted at 07:41:38 (0@89) and again at 07:41:49 (0@93). Both postings came after the naive-handler deploy.

proposed_fix.summary:
1. Roll ledger-consumer back to its previous image and settings, with a LEDGER_HANDLER that dedupes on event_id.
2. As a separate data repair, add compensating reversals for the extra transactions, keeping the first posting of each event: reverse 292 (evt_000288), 319 (evt_000298), 322 and 323 (evt_000308), 359 (evt_000352) and 381 (evt_000373).
3. Rerun the money check.

diagnosis.blast_radius:
The rollback restarts ledger-consumer, so ledger posting pauses briefly and resumes from committed offsets. payment-confirmer and payments-api are untouched.

The data repair changes ledger balances. Reversing the wrong transaction would create a new mismatch. Duplicates posted after this money check may also need the same repair.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If the rolled-back handler fails to consume, redeploy ledger-consumer with the current image and settings. The reversals are compensating transactions, not deletes, so they can be undone by voiding them.
